extracted.intended_audience: readers, donors, community members, and prospective staff of Honolulu Civil Beat (local news consumers and supporters)
extracted.subtask_description: An 'About' summary describing a local nonprofit newsroom's mission, editorial and ethical standards, funding transparency, and community engagement practices used to produce and evaluate journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — engage and educate the community
rubrics_metrics.description: Our mission is to engage and educate the community on important public issues through in-depth reporting, explanatory and investigative journalism, analysis and commentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce journalism with a purpose to stimulate positive change; aim to cultivate an informed body of citizens and make Hawaiʻi a better place to live.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watchdog role — challenge leaders and protect public trust
rubrics_metrics.description: We are the watchdogs of the public’s trust and we take seriously the mission to educate our citizens on important public issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The newsroom's goal is to challenge our leaders to do better and to investigate wrongdoing, spotlight important issues, and serve as a voice for those who feel they have none.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence — no alignment with political or special interest groups
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not align with political or special interest groups and adhere to the strictest journalistic standards and ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain independence in reporting and decision-making; funding relationships should not compromise editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to professional ethics and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, we follow the guidelines set out by the Society of Professional Journalists in its ethics code as well as more general news practices outlined by the Associated Press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SPJ ethics code and AP practices as the baseline for newsroom decisions; links to specific policies (ethics code, AP practices) are provided for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of anonymous sources — rare and narrowly justified
rubrics_metrics.description: When We (Rarely) Use Anonymous Sources: We rely on anonymous sources only when we think the information is important and we couldn’t get it otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymous sourcing should be an exception; newsroom policy governs when anonymity is acceptable and requires justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections policy — transparency and truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Corrections Policy: Transparency and truth. Those are our commitments. Our policy on how to handle corrections is central to both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a clear, public corrections policy; correct mistakes transparently and prominently according to the stated policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding transparency and donor ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: We are committed to transparency in every aspect of funding our small nonprofit newsroom. View our list of supporters and learn about our donor ethics guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose major donors (e.g., Omidyar ʻOhana Fund support), list supporters publicly, and publish donor ethics guidelines to explain how funding is handled and how editorial independence is protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of news — reader-supported, paywall removed
rubrics_metrics.description: To expand our reach so that more people in Hawaiʻi have access to the information they need, Civil Beat removed its paywall in June 2016 and transitioned to 501(c)3 nonprofit status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor broad public access to reporting (e.g., no paywall) as part of mission to treat news as a public asset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community forums and civil discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide a number of different forums for a broad range of news, views and commentary where citizens can debate the issues in a civil manner, free from cheap shots and personal swipes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host public events, newsletters, Facebook groups, and other forums; moderate to encourage civil debate and prevent personal attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community engagement through events and newsletters
rubrics_metrics.description: Besides publishing CivilBeat.org, we hold regular public events including Civil Cafes, Pop-Up Newsrooms and Hawaiʻi Storytellers. Our Morning Beat newsletter is emailed to tens of thousands of subscribers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use events and newsletters to extend reporting impact, foster community discussion, and increase reach and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability via public financial disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Honolulu Civil Beat’s Form 990: [years listed]. Employer Identification Number (EIN): 81-2803662.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish tax forms and financial identifiers to allow public scrutiny of nonprofit finances and demonstrate accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness and accuracy in community-contributed content
rubrics_metrics.description: Community Voices: Fairness and accuracy are important in this highly popular section. Here's how to do it and what to keep in mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set and communicate standards for submissions to community/opinion sections to ensure fairness, accuracy, and quality; provide guidance to contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility signaled by awards and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil Beat has won numerous local, regional and national journalism awards, including a finalist for the Pulitzer Prize in 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and publicize independent awards and honors as indicators of journalistic quality and impact.
